title: Age has not withered it. Beauty and peace have not done it away. It is in infinite variety everywhere
html_source:
In Antony and Cleopatra, Act II, Scene 2, Domitus Enobarbus praises Cleopatra, observing that Antony will never leave her because:

“Age cannot wither her, nor custom stale
Her infinite variety”

Stephen is arguing that Shakespeare’s evergreen theme is Anne Hathaway’s infidelity, which he categorizes as “banishment.” Stephen cites literal banishment and includes betrayal or infidelity or unrequited love as varieties of banishment. These things are found throughout Shakespeare, although Stephen throws a pretty broad net.

Also, Joyce uses this sort of “banishment” as a theme in Ulysses, through, among other things, the centrality of Molly’s infidelity to Bloom with Boylan.
